scope: Fifteen school-neutral, reproducible real-data projects with one distinct substantive case per private application-program mapping.

cases.title: Jersey City Bike Demand and Rebalancing Evidence
cases.gallery_title: Jersey City Bike Demand and Rebalancing Evidence
cases.question: Can station-hour history improve held-out pickup forecasts, and which fixed-budget rebalancing scenario deserves a bounded operations pilot?

source.dataset: Jersey City Bike Demand and Rebalancing Evidence
source.version: Jersey City trip history, January-December 2021; derived station-hour aggregate

cases.result: Held-out station-hour MAE is 0.69 pickups/day, a 33.1% improvement over the hour-only baseline.
cases.boundary: Rebalancing outcomes are modeled; no stockout, routing, labor, or achieved-service claim.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Jersey City Bike Demand and Rebalancing Evidence

cases.title: Cross-City 311 Distribution Shift and Transfer Gate
cases.gallery_title: Cross-City 311 Distribution Shift and Transfer Gate
cases.question: Are city service-request distributions sufficiently comparable to transfer an analytical rule between Chicago and New York?

source.dataset: Cross-City 311 Distribution Shift and Transfer Gate
source.publisher: City of Chicago and City of New York

cases.result: The 2023 cross-city total-variation distance is 58.1%, and the transfer gate is refused.
cases.boundary: Administrative shift audit only; requests are not latent need or service quality.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Cross-City 311 Distribution Shift and Transfer Gate

cases.title: Capacity-Constrained Marketing Pilot
cases.question: Can pre-contact information concentrate observed responses under a fixed outreach capacity without using post-contact leakage?
cases.result: The untouched test yields an AUC of 0.650 and a Brier score of 0.210; the top 5% captures 7.4% of observed responses.
cases.boundary: Observed response concentration is not incremental lift, causal treatment effect, profit, or return on outreach.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Capacity-Constrained Marketing Pilot

cases.title: ACS Employment AI Temporal Transport and Audit
cases.gallery_title: ACS Employment AI Temporal Transport and Audit
cases.gallery_endpoint: do not use for consequential action
cases.question: How well does a protected-attribute-excluded employment model developed on 2019 PUMS transport to 2023?

source.dataset: ACS Employment AI Temporal Transport and Audit
source.version: Rhode Island ACS 1-year PUMS person files, 2019 and 2023
source.grain: one working-age ACS PUMS person record

cases.result: The untouched 2023 temporal test yields an AUC of 0.640 and a weighted Brier score of 0.158.
cases.terminal_output: do not use for consequential action
cases.boundary: No eligibility, hiring, credit, benefits, or other consequential action.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for ACS Employment AI Temporal Transport and Audit

cases.title: Treasury Curve and Tail-Risk Decision Engine
cases.gallery_title: Treasury Curve and Tail-Risk Decision Engine
cases.question: How do duration choices change historical tail loss, backtest behavior, and sensitivity to dependent market shocks?

source.dataset: Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates
source.grain: one U.S. Treasury business-day yield curve

methods: daily carry plus first-order duration response
cases.result: Historical ES95 loss rises from 0.4% for the short baseline to 0.9% for the long-duration portfolio; the short-baseline rolling VaR exceedance rate is 6.0%.
cases.boundary: First-order duration omits convexity, security selection, costs, financing, taxes, liquidity, and future-regime uncertainty.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Treasury Curve and Tail-Risk Decision Engine

cases.title: Human-in-the-Loop Complaint Triage Information System
cases.question: Does a privacy-minimized complaint model create reliable ranking gain over random review in a later calendar period?

source.dataset: Consumer Complaint Database: Money Transfer, Virtual Currency, or Money Service
source.version: Closed 2022 UTC date window; privacy-minimized extract created 2026-07-27
source.grain: one CFPB complaint received in 2022 for a money-transfer, virtual-currency, or money-service product

cases.result: The later-period AUC is 0.611 (block-bootstrap 95% interval 0.539 to 0.697), while top-5% lift is 1.00 (95% interval 0.33 to 2.46); the ranking model fails the deployment gate.
cases.boundary: The timely flag is not complaint merit, harm, resolution quality, company quality, or compliance; the 2022 model may not transport.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Human-in-the-Loop Complaint Triage Information System

cases.title: Commercial Real Estate Diligence Decision Product
cases.gallery_title: Commercial Real Estate Diligence Decision Product
cases.question: Which borough/property-type segments have enough public transaction evidence for property-level diligence, and how do financing-rate assumptions change the income hurdle?

source.dataset: Commercial Real Estate Transactions and Regeneration Risk
source.publisher: New York City Department of Finance via NYC Open Data
source.version: filtered 2021-2025 commercial-unit snapshot from dataset w2pb-icbu
source.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use
source.grain: one public NYC property-sale record before robust analytical filtering

cases.result: Across 12,399 filtered commercial transactions, Manhattan has the highest borough median price per square foot at $743; the break-even cap rate at 8.5% debt is 7.5%.
cases.boundary: The source does not establish arm's-length status, NOI, expenses, occupancy, condition, appraisal value, debt terms, or causal regeneration effects.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Commercial Real Estate Diligence Decision Product

cases.title: Wildfire Mitigation Evidence Allocation Under Uncertainty
cases.gallery_title: Wildfire Mitigation Evidence Allocation Under Uncertainty
cases.question: Which exposure-weighted evidence-collection allocation is least fragile across historical, recent, and tail-fire scenarios?

source.dataset: Wildfire Mitigation Evidence Allocation Under Uncertainty
source.publisher: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
source.version: California Historic Fire Perimeters feature service, filtered to 2000-2025

cases.result: Across 8,892 valid mapped perimeters, recent observed acres is the lowest-regret proxy allocation under the tested scenarios.
cases.boundary: No fires-prevented or acres-prevented estimate; mitigation action blocked pending effectiveness and feasibility evidence.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Wildfire Mitigation Evidence Allocation Under Uncertainty

cases.title: SEC N-PORT Liquidity and Crowding Filing Review
cases.gallery_title: SEC N-PORT Liquidity and Crowding Filing Review
cases.question: Which transparent concentration, liquidity, and redemption indicators should trigger targeted filing review?

source.dataset: SEC N-PORT Liquidity and Crowding Filing Review
source.version: Form N-PORT Data Set 2025 Q4, minimized to fund-level review indicators

cases.result: Across 11,747 reviewed filings, median top-10 holding concentration is 34.5% and the 90th-percentile Level-3 share is 0.2%.
cases.boundary: Filing review only; no expected-return, suitability, fund-quality, or investment recommendation.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for SEC N-PORT Liquidity and Crowding Filing Review

cases.title: Social-Norm Field Experiment with Household-Clustered Inference
cases.gallery_title: Social-Norm Field Experiment with Household-Clustered Inference
cases.gallery_endpoint: observed field effect no new campaign authorization
cases.question: What were the intent-to-treat turnout effects of randomized social-pressure mailings after household clustering?

source.dataset: Social-Norm Field Experiment with Household-Clustered Inference
source.publisher: Yale Institution for Social and Policy Studies
source.version: Gerber-Green-Larimer 2008 replication file; non-identifying aggregate and locally computed clustered inference

cases.result: The Neighbors arm has the largest observed intent-to-treat effect at 8.1%, with a household-clustered 95% interval of 7.5% to 8.8%.
cases.terminal_output: observed field effect no new campaign authorization
cases.boundary: Causal scope is the historical randomized experiment; no new campaign authorization.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Social-Norm Field Experiment with Household-Clustered Inference

cases.title: Population Health Risk Transport Across NHIS Cohorts
cases.gallery_title: Population Health Risk Transport Across NHIS Cohorts
cases.question: Do simple population-risk cells developed in NHIS 2016 retain discrimination and calibration in the 2017 linked-mortality cohort?

source.dataset: Population Health Risk Transport Across NHIS Cohorts
source.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics
source.version: NHIS 2016 and 2017 Sample Adult files linked to 2019 public-use mortality
source.grain: one NHIS sampled adult linked to mortality status

cases.result: The 2017 temporal test yields an AUC of 0.846 and weighted two-year mortality of 2.32% across 58,754 linked adults.
cases.boundary: Population-risk validation only; no individual diagnosis, treatment, or clinical deployment.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Population Health Risk Transport Across NHIS Cohorts

cases.title: Opportunity Zone One-Year Policy Evidence Screen
cases.gallery_title: Opportunity Zone One-Year Policy Evidence Screen
cases.question: How did selected tract outcomes change immediately after QOZ designation relative to observed-covariate matches?

source.dataset: Opportunity Zone One-Year Policy Evidence Screen
source.publisher: CDFI Fund and U.S. Census Bureau
source.version: 2018 designated QOZ list with 2018-2019 ACS and LODES Massachusetts tract panel

cases.result: The matched one-year screen contains 1,460 complete tract panels, including 138 designated QOZ tracts and 121 unique matched controls.
cases.boundary: Associational one-year screen; no causal effect because parallel trends are unavailable.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Opportunity Zone One-Year Policy Evidence Screen

cases.title: Small-Sample Repeated-Measures Inference
cases.question: How does passage type change eye-movement burden within the same participant, and how stable is the contrast across reader groups?

source.dataset: Eye movements of dyslexic and average readers in meaningful and pseudoword passage reading
source.grain: one de-identified study participant with repeated passage measures

cases.result: Across 57 complete participant pairs, the mean pseudoword-minus-meaningful fixation-duration difference is 34.25 (bootstrap 95% interval 25.87 to 43.35), with a Holm-adjusted sign-flip p-value of 0.0003.
cases.boundary: The public sample is small and does not establish downstream educational outcomes or an intervention effect.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Small-Sample Repeated-Measures Inference

cases.title: NHANES Mortality Transportability and Population Inequality
cases.gallery_title: NHANES Mortality Transportability and Population Inequality
cases.question: Do population mortality risk patterns transport between NHANES cohorts, and what inequality gradient remains visible?

source.dataset: NHANES Mortality Transportability and Population Inequality
source.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics
source.version: NHANES 2011-2012 and 2015-2016 demographics linked to 2019 mortality
source.grain: one NHANES adult linked to 36-month mortality

cases.result: The external-cohort check yields an AUC of 0.804 and a Brier score of 0.022 across 11,820 linked adults.
cases.boundary: Population research only; no individual diagnosis or treatment.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for NHANES Mortality Transportability and Population Inequality

cases.title: Spatial Equity Planning with Transit and Site-Evidence Gates
cases.gallery_title: Spatial Equity Planning with Transit and Site-Evidence Gates
cases.question: Which tract-level service-hub priorities merit local review after observed rapid-transit proximity is added?

source.dataset: Spatial Equity Planning with Transit and Site-Evidence Gates
source.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau and Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority
source.version: 2019-2023 ACS tract estimates, 2023 Gazetteer, and MBTA rapid-transit stops accessed 2026-08-10
source.license: U.S. Government open data and MBTA open data

headline_metrics.label: Site decision
headline_metrics.value: blocked pending land and feasibility evidence

cases.result: Across 1,597 analyzed tracts and 265 rapid-transit stop records, the high-poverty weighted nearest-stop distance is 40.65 km.
cases.boundary: No site recommendation until parcel, zoning, network, cost, and community evidence is supplied.
